This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The land bearing Sy.No.61/1 measuring 1 acre 10 guntas situated at Bodanayakadinni village,
Bagalkot Taluk and District, belonging to the petitioners was acquired for the purpose of Timmapur Lift Irrigation Project.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer passed an award determining the compensation at Rs.1,458.89 per gunta i.e. Rs.58,356/- per acre.

Dis -satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded, the petitioners filed a petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer vide order dated 16.6.2020 enhanced the compensation to Rs.8,51,000/- per acre, however, denied the interest from the date of registration of reference application till disposal stating that the claimants protracted the proceedings by remaining absent.
Taking exception to the denial of interest till disposal, this petition is filed.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioners - claimants submits that the Reference Court had committed an error in denying the interest from the date of registration of the reference application till closure of the evidence and from the NC: 2024:KHC-D:902 date of restoration till disposal of the reference application.
Therefore, the impugned award passed by the Reference Court requires to be quashed insofar as it relates to the denial of interest.

To substantiate that the petition under Article 226 is maintainable against the order refusing to grant interest, he places reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India -vs- Pushpavathi (AIR 2018 SC 1032).
3.

The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State submits that the claimants having protracted the proceedings, the claimants are not entitled for interest and the Reference Court rightly passed the impugned award, which does not warrant any interference.
4. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 5. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India (supra) has held that the dispute in relation to the non- award of interest can be raised by an aggrieved person only by taking recourse of Article 226 of the Constitution and Section 18 or Section 28A(3) cannot be considered to be alternative statutory remedy available to landowner questioning the non- award of interest payable under Sections 28 or 34 of the Act decided by Civil Court.
6. The reference application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act was registered on 17.6.2015.

The matter was listed for tendering of evidence by the claimants on NC:
2024:KHC-D:902 11.1.2016 and the matter was closed on 19.7.2017, since the claimants did not appear to tender evidence, and the same was re-opened on 2.3.2020.
The protracting of the proceedings on the part of the claimants is from 19.7.2017 till 2.3.2020 i.e. when the matter was re-opened and the claimants are permitted to tender evidence.
Therefore, the Reference Court instead of denying the interest for the said period has denied the interest from the date of registration till disposal and the same is not sustainable in law.
Since the claimants have lost their valuable lands, they are entitled for statutory interest as provided under the Act.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 16.6.2020 passed by the II Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and JMFC, Bagalkot, Bagalkot in LAC No.33/2015
insofar as it relates denying the interest to the claimants from the date of registration of the reference application till disposal is hereby quashed.
iii) The claimants are not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation from 19.7.2017 till 2.3.2020 and other portion of the award is unaltered.
